# Dark Magic

*Pages PDF 62-63*

_And lo, he shall rule with a dark hand, and his shadow shall touch upon every land. Steel will be his skin, and fire will be his blood. In hatred will he conquer all before him … will it come to pass that the firstborn son of noble blood shall rise to power. The child will be learned in the darkest arts and he will raise an army of terrible beasts. Thus will the Dark King fall, slain by neither blade nor arrow but by a sorcerous power of darkest magic, and so shall his body be consumed in the flames and for all eternity burn._ 

The Dread King knows of the Prophecy of Demise and believes it is he to whom the prophecy refers. He is determined to escape that destiny, hence his persecution of male sorcerers. 

Despite the danger of being outlawed for doing so, some dark elf lords surreptitiously employ male sorcerers. They run the risk of earning Malerion’s wrath, and the punishment he would order would be severe, but on the other hand, there is always a price to pay for the aid of the sorceresses of the Dark Convent. 

## **The Dark Convent and Covens**
Chief among the magic-wielders of Naggaroth are the sisters of the Dark Convent of Sorceresses who gather in the great fortress of Ghrond. Competition for positions in the Dark Convent is bloody and fierce. Those who survive their sisters’ attentions learn some of the most powerful magic in the world. 

Sooner or later, however, differing magical interests, old rivalries, and political manoeuvring see collaboration break down in favour of conflict. Given their reluctance to act directly against one another, members of a coven rely on agents and careful manipulation to make plays against their peers. 

There is no shortage of acolytes and toadies who hope to win favour with sorceresses, and so the network of sorceresses’ pawns extends everywhere in Druchii society and beyond. 

## **The Silent Walkers**
Sorceress Netathi Fellwhisper spends hours in her chambers on _Temple of Spite_ researching a complex magical ritual to bind minor daemons into living creatures. By trapping them in these vessels, she hopes to exert control over the daemons and use them to syphon off the harmful effects of _Dhar_ . Early test subjects can be found wandering the corridors of the ark, their tongues mutilated and their eyes staring at things no one else can see. Fellwhisper assumes they are failures, no more than soulless husks. This is only partly true — in fact, a herald of Tzeentch is splintered across their broken minds. rival sorceress rakaria Dran discovered one of the captives and realised that should at least four come together, they could open a channel to something beyond mortal comprehension. Dran needs help to track down the remaining six vessels. 

Founded by Morathi and Anethra Helbane when Ghrond was new, the Dark Convent is where fledgling aspirants are forged into sorceresses, and the screams from their trials echo through the streets at all hours. It is a place of horrors and wonders in equal measure, and looms in the nightmares of young Druchii girls who first feel the stirrings of magical awakening. 

Nearly all Druchii girls with magical potential are sent to Ghrond where, should they overcome the torturous challenges to master dark magic, prestige and power alike are guaranteed. Dark elf families gladly offer up their daughters to the Convent, hopeful for advantage, though few sorceresses retain a sense of obligation to their family. 

Individual covens are alliances between sorceresses, assigned to fulfil particular designs by Morathi or one of her supreme sorceresses. Covens cooperate for mutual advantage, and the sorceresses are wildly individualistic, though intelligent and manipulative enough to appreciate the value of collaboration where necessary. 

## **Dark Magic**
Novice magic users find dark magic dangerously simple to use, but using it effectively is a challenging act of force. Its wielders wrangle the raw essence of magic into a congealed mass, bending it to their whims by sheer power of will. The resulting energy is a discordant mingling of winds, close in essence to the raw stuff of Chaos. 

All magic is risky, though the dangers are much greater with _Dhar_ for, as a mingling of different winds, it pulls in multiple metaphysical directions simultaneously. It is a potent contradiction, an amalgamation of opposites that shapes the world in impossible ways, leading to mutation and madness. Most magical practice only produces _Dhar_ by mistake; a gifted child trying their first petty conjurations might pull several winds together, or an unschooled witch could draw on strands of magic indiscriminately. Skilled practitioners, by contrast, use _Dhar_ intentionally, to force this unruly source of power towards deliberate ends. 

Dark Magic 

## **Corruption and Miscasts**
When making a Casting Test for a Spell from the Lore of Dark Magic, or when using Channelling ( _Dhar_ ), treat all Miscast results as Major Miscasts, unless the caster has the _Instinctive Diction_ Talent. Ingredients have no effect on reducing the severity of a Miscast. 

A Lore of Dark Magic Spell is a Corrupting Influence in itself, so any roll of an 8 on the units die when making a casting test for a Spell from the Lore of Dark Magic, or when using Channelling ( _Dhar_ ), results in a Major Miscast and the caster gains 1 Corruption Point. The act of casting a Spell from the Lore of Dark Magic moves an elf towards Dark Yenlui (see **High Elf Players’ Guide** , page 46). 

Dark elf sorceresses and sorcerers use soul pacts to offset the risk of using dark magic. 

## **Dark Magic Complications**
Wizards who meddle with dark magic find that excess _Dhar_ soaks into reality and warps the world around them. When a Lore of Dark Magic Spell is dispelled, a Ritual interrupted without completion, or every time a Casting Test exceeds +4 SL above the Casting Number, roll for a Complication. 

## **Soul Pacts**
Many dark magic spells are tightly controlled acts of daemonology. Sorceresses call on sinister entities to devour their enemies, manifest vortexes of dark energy, or hurl storms of wicked shards at their foes. 

Sorceresses mitigate Corruption and Major Miscasts by brokering pacts with beings that have mastery over the essence of dark magic. For most sorceresses, this is Hekarti, who has dominion over sorcery, though others try to invoke a Chaos Power or daemon prince through their heralds and daemonic agents. More often than not, the hidden hand behind these agents is the Dark Prince, Slaanesh. Sorceresses make pacts with multiple entities, often to protect themselves from the claim made by other daemons on their soul. The most exalted sorceresses’ souls are held together only by dark bargains and sheer willpower. 

All daemons and gods demand sacrifices as part of their bargain: Hekarti desires victims slain by magic, and prefers such victims to be spellcasters themselves, while other entities have peculiar and diverse demands. Sorceresses are arrogant, and most do not see themselves as worshippers or followers, though even then they know they must eventually pay their side of the bargain. 

## **Talent: Soul Pact**
## **Max:** 4
Only elves may take this Talent. Using rituals, sacrifice, and careful negotiation, the magic user has bargained with a dark entity to protect them from the worst effects of _Dhar_ on their body and soul. They must continue to placate the entity, who hungers for their soul and demands ever more sacrifice with each passing year. When they cast Spells from the Lore of Dark Magic, they can invest any Overcast SL in protecting themself from Corruption, see **Sorceress Pacts** on page 64. Each time they take this Talent, they can make another pact.
